findings.title: New fallback behavior ships with no tests
findings.body: This PR changes core translation resolution (custom `I18n.fallbacks`, on-demand loading of the fallback chain, removal of Rails' `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` in production/profile/cloud66) but adds no tests. The behavior is subtle and easy to regress: fallback ordering (user locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en), deduplication, behavior when the default locale is unavailable, and the interaction with the LRU cache in `I18n.translate` are all untested. A maintainer cannot verify that `I18n.t` for a key missing in the current locale now returns the default-locale/en string (and that missing keys still raise/return 'translation missing' when nothing exists). Add specs for these paths.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only preloaded inside controller requests
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is invoked only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so the fallback chain (current locale, `SiteSetting.default_locale`, `:en`) is loaded only during web requests. Outside requests — background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console — `I18n.translate` (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68) loads only `config.locale`, and the `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` translation path calls `super` for fallback locales without triggering `load_locale` for them. Result: in those contexts a key missing from the active locale may resolve to 'translation missing' instead of the intended default-locale/`:en` string, because those locale files were never loaded in that process. Loading the fallback chain should happen centrally (e.g., in the patched `I18n.translate`/`ensure_loaded!`, or an initializer), not solely in a controller filter.

findings.title: Inconsistent and fragile backend include target for fallbacks
findings.body: Pluralization is mixed into `I18n::Backend::Simple` directly (line 5), but fallbacks are mixed into `I18n.backend.class` (line 9). This forces eager instantiation of `I18n.backend` at initializer time and, more importantly, means fallbacks are only attached to whichever backend class happens to be active during this initializer. If `I18n.backend` is later replaced (e.g., by a Chain backend in some environment or a future change), the `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` module silently drops off and fallbacks stop working with no error. Use the same explicit `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` form used for pluralization (or otherwise guarantee the included backend is the one actually used).

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but only overrides `[]`, breaking standard Fallbacks API
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks` is normally an `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, which exposes `[]`, `[]=`, `key?`, `fetch`, `each`, `to_h`, `defaults`, etc. `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` stores no keys and only overrides `[]`, so any code (current or in future i18n gem internals) that iterates `I18n.fallbacks`, checks `key?`, or relies on the stored mapping will see an empty Hash and behave incorrectly. Subclass `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` and override `[]` instead, so the object remains a real fallbacks collection while still customizing the chain.
